title: Anthropic Sets $1.5T IPO Price, Ukraine's Allies Meet in Berlin as Trump, Xi, and Putin Shake Hands in Shenzhen, and Myanmar Reviews ASEAN Ties
subhead: Anthropic prices its landmark IPO at $83 per share as Donald Trump, Xi Jinping, and Vladimir Putin exchange handshakes in Shenzhen, European allies and US envoys convene in Berlin on Ukraine, and Myanmar signals a rethink of ASEAN ties.

sections.heading: Anthropic Prices IPO at $83 per Share for $1.5T Valuation
sections.body:
AI model developer Anthropic priced its initial public offering at $83 per share on Wednesday evening, above its projected range, valuing the five-year-old firm at $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis, AP News, BBC, and Le Monde report. Strong institutional demand pushed pricing upward ahead of Thursday's trading debut, even as Bloomberg notes Asian equities slipped ahead of the listing and Anthropic raised $3 billion in its Japanese tranche at the lower end of that segment's range.

The public debut arrives alongside wider debate over AI governance and US tech leadership at the New York Times DealBook Summit. CNBC and the BBC report Elon Musk called former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang 'irreplaceable'—while saying Musk's own near-$500 million midterm spending was 'pretty foolish' and declaring he is 'not MAGA'—as the New York Times details how Alibaba-linked entities brought Nvidia chips within reach of China's military.
sections.whyItMatters: Anthropic's $1.5 trillion debut tests public-market appetite for frontier AI laboratories at the exact moment semiconductor export enforcement and Nvidia's leadership turmoil have rattled tech valuations.

sections.heading: Trump, Xi, and Putin Shake Hands in Shenzhen Ahead of Trilateral Talks
sections.body:
Chinese President Xi Jinping greeted US President Donald Trump on the tarmac in Shenzhen before Xi, Trump, and Russian President Vladimir Putin exchanged handshakes ahead of a rare three-way meeting on the sidelines of the APEC summit, the New York Times, CBS News, and France 24 report. In public remarks at the summit, Anadolu Agency notes Xi called for advancing the Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific as a shared APEC vision.

Washington and Beijing are using the summit to manage multiple friction points simultaneously. SCMP reports the US conducted an unarmed intercontinental ballistic missile test hours before Air Force One landed in China, while Anadolu Agency reports South Korean President Lee and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi held their first separate meetings with Putin on the summit sidelines. Meanwhile, Trump told Americans to 'relax' over recent US bank, airline, and tech outages, calling them 'individual events,' Anadolu Agency writes.
sections.whyItMatters: Putting Trump, Xi, and Putin in the same room creates an unusual high-level channel to address trade, nuclear arms stability, and ongoing wars, though parallel ICBM testing underscores lingering strategic distrust.

sections.heading: Ukraine's Allies Convene in Berlin After Second Kerch Bridge Attack
sections.body:
Ukraine's European backers gathered in Berlin on Thursday for a 'Coalition of the Willing' summit joined by US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, DW reports, as allies weigh security guarantees and diplomatic terms for Kyiv. On the battlefield, Anadolu Agency cites the Moscow-installed head of Crimea confirming traffic remained suspended on the Kerch Bridge after a second Ukrainian drone attack caused damage and triggered a structural assessment.

Meanwhile, Gulf security pressures persisted alongside the European talks. CBS News reports Iran stepped up attacks on Persian Gulf allies and tankers after US strikes, while the Times of Israel notes Houthi forces claimed cruise missile attacks on Riyadh's international airport and finance center, and Trump claimed there are indications Iran is 'looking at' biological weapons. Separately, Anadolu Agency reports Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman met CENTCOM's commander in Riyadh to review military cooperation.
sections.whyItMatters: Simultaneous diplomacy in Berlin and Shenzhen highlights a widening split between allied coordination on Ukraine's defense and direct US-Russia-China talks over war termination.

sections.heading: Myanmar Reviews ASEAN Ties Ahead of ICJ Rohingya Genocide Ruling
sections.body:
Myanmar's military-backed leader Min Aung Hlaing announced his administration is reconsidering its future relationship with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) over perceived 'indignity,' though it will continue bilateral talks with member states, SCMP reports. The warning comes just as the International Court of Justice prepares to rule on The Gambia's genocide case against Myanmar over the 2017 military crackdown that displaced at least 730,000 Rohingya, Al Jazeera reports.

At the COP31 climate summit, France 24 reports Vanuatu Environment Minister Ralph Regenvanu called for urgent reform of the UN climate negotiation process, accusing a small bloc of nations of stalling progress and warning COP31 risks reversing earlier commitments. In the Pacific, AFP notes Fiji declared a national drought crisis driven by El Nino.
sections.whyItMatters: Myanmar's threat to pull back from ASEAN ahead of an ICJ genocide verdict threatens to deepen Southeast Asia's diplomatic deadlock over border security, refugees, and regional legitimacy.

sections.heading: Florida Pastor Convicted in 2021 Assassination of Haiti's President
sections.body:
A federal jury in Miami convicted 67-year-old Florida pastor Christian Emmanuel Sanon for his role in the 2021 assassination plot against Haitian President Jovenel Moise, exposing him to a potential life sentence, the New York Times and Le Monde report. The assassination plunged Haiti into years of institutional collapse and armed gang violence that has since drawn Salvadoran security forces into Port-au-Prince.

In US domestic politics, CNBC reports Democrat Mary Peltola defeated incumbent Republican Dan Sullivan in Alaska's Senate race, locking in a 56-44 Democratic Senate majority starting in January, while The Hill notes Republican Rep. Nick Begich held Alaska's lone House seat. Elsewhere, CNBC reports Google removed 19,000 Indonesian pro-government YouTube channels, and NBC News notes a Virginia school district shut through Thanksgiving after discovering 500 staff had not been screened for child abuse.
sections.whyItMatters: A US conviction in the Moise assassination brings rare legal accountability to Haiti's destabilization, while final US midterm results clarify the 56-seat Democratic Senate majority that will shape legislation in 2027.

bottomLine: Anthropic's $1.5 trillion IPO pricing, the Shenzhen handshake among Trump, Xi, and Putin, and Berlin's Ukraine summit frame a day where capital markets and great-power diplomacy intersect directly. With Gulf missile alerts, renewed strikes on the Kerch Bridge, and Myanmar's challenge to ASEAN unfolding in parallel, investors and governments alike are watching whether Shenzhen produces concrete de-escalation or deeper bloc fragmentation.
sources: AP News, BBC, Le Monde, CNBC, New York Times, CBS News, France 24, Anadolu Agency, SCMP, DW, Al Jazeera, Times of Israel, The Hill, NBC News
